meta.notes: SINGLE-FILER FIGURES verified 2026-08-15 against the statutory text at law.lis.virginia.gov. Brackets are NOT filing-status dependent: 58.1-320 imposes the rates on 'every individual', so there is no single bracket table and none is needed. standardDeductionSingle/ByYear is exactly half the MFJ schedule at every step ($8,750 TY2025-2026, $9,200 TY2027, $9,300 TY2028-2029, reverting to $3,000 from TY2030). vaExemptions are already per person ($930 each plus $800 per person 65+), so a one-person household simply claims one — no single-specific value exists or is needed. THE ONE NON-PROPORTIONAL FIGURE is the age-deduction threshold: 58.1-322.03(5.b) reads '$50,000 for single taxpayers or $75,000 for married taxpayers', so afagiThresholdSingle is $50,000 and NOT half of $75,000 — a widow starts losing the $12,000 age deduction $25,000 of income sooner than a halving rule predicts. Verified 2026-08-12 (tax.virginia.gov, law.lis.virginia.gov 58.1-322.03). Brackets statutory, not indexed. Standard deduction MFJ is a legislated schedule (2026 Appropriation Act amending 58.1-322.03): $17,500 TY2025-2026, $18,400 TY2027, $18,600 TY2028-2029, with a statutory reversion to $6,000 from TY2030 — standardDeductionMfjByYear carries the enacted schedule and standardDeductionMfj ($6,000) is the post-2029 current-law fallback for years beyond it. Virginia has repeatedly extended the elevated deduction before each sunset; to assume another extension, raise the fallback (and/or extend the schedule). Age deduction: $12,000 per person 65+ (born after Jan 1 1939), reduced $1-for-$1 by combined AFAGI over $75,000 MFJ, where AFAGI = federal AGI minus federally-taxed Social Security. SS fully subtracted.
